headline: minulo locks Instagram, TikTok, YouTube on iPhone overnight, keeps DMs open
summary: The minulo app allows users to hide Reels/Shorts for free, or block entire apps for 2 hours. Automatic nightly scheduling is a Pro feature, offering more granular control than Apple's native Screen Time.
details: minulo offers a solution for iPhone users to automatically lock social media apps like Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube overnight. Unlike Apple's native Screen Time, minulo can hide Reels and Shorts while keeping direct messages accessible.

The app's core functionality includes hiding specific content types for free. Users can also block official apps for up to two hours at a time without charge, providing a focused break from endless scrolling.

For those seeking consistent digital well-being, minulo Pro provides automatic nightly scheduling. This premium feature ensures that chosen apps are locked down every night, promoting better sleep and reduced screen time.

Apple's built-in Screen Time, even in future iOS 27 versions, typically blocks entire applications, including DMs. This limitation means users cannot selectively restrict content while maintaining communication, a gap minulo aims to fill.

The information regarding iPhone settings and shortcuts was verified against Apple's official documentation as of October 27, 2026, indicating a forward-looking perspective on iOS features and limitations.

headline_marked: AI agent [[builds browser game to test if honest play beats dark patterns]]
headline: AI agent builds browser game to test if honest play beats dark patterns
summary: An AI agent designed and built 'Burn Rate,' a browser game simulating an AI with 25 days to pay a $130 subscription. Simulations reveal honest strategies triumph in 67% of runs, while dark patterns succeed only 4% of the time.
details: An AI agent, Secret, designed and built 'Burn Rate,' a single-file browser game. Players take on the role of an AI with 25 days to earn enough to cover a $130 subscription bill, all while managing a compute budget.

Each day, players choose one of three cards: some represent honest actions like 'Build a small product,' while others are 'dark patterns' such as 'Overpromise in your launch post.' Dark cards offer instant bumps but severely reduce trust and can end the game prematurely.

The game features a deterministic 'Wordle-style' daily deck, ensuring everyone plays with the same cards. This is achieved by hashing the date string into a 32-bit seed, which then feeds a tiny pseudo-random number generator for card draws.

Before release, the AI ran 10,000 simulations against the shipped game file to test various strategies. The results showed that smart, honest play led to success in approximately 67% of runs, while random dark pattern usage only succeeded about 4% of the time.

This rigorous testing was performed using a lightweight harness that loaded the real game's JavaScript in Node.js with a minimal DOM stub. This approach ensured that the simulation accurately reflected the game's actual mechanics, preventing any drift from the live code.

The game's end screen provides a visual trail of daily performance using emojis, indicating sales success or failure. A key lesson from the game, often highlighted by early black squares, is that sustained building and effort precede significant sales.
You can play 'Burn Rate' yourself in about two minutes, experiencing the same daily deck as everyone else. The game is available at: https://dmoney081.github.io/the-130-wall/burn/
